evidence.title: NPTEL Applied Elasticity, Chapter 9, equations 9.47, 9.50, 9.78-9.92
evidence.finding: Derives the dimensional Prandtl stress-function formulation and rectangular trigonometric/hyperbolic series; division by material/twist scale gives the normalized -2 equation.

Normalizing dimensional stress function Phi by G times twist-per-length gives phi with Laplacian -2. After a quadratic particular solution, harmonic separated corrections combine cos(k*x) with cosh(k*y) or sinh(k*y).

The -2 convention is a normalized torsion function, not an unscaled stress potential. The simple zero boundary value is for a homogeneous isotropic simply connected section such as the rectangle; multiply connected or restrained-warping problems require additional conditions.
